description_full: ZoomInfo Technologies Inc., together with its subsidiaries, provides go-to-market intelligence and engagement platform for sales, marketing, operations, and recruiting professionals in the United States and internationally. The company's cloud-based platform provides workflow tools and information on organizations and professionals to help users identify target customers and decision makers, obtain continually updated predictive lead and company scoring, monitor buying signals and other attributes of target companies, craft messages, engage through automated sales tools, and track progress through the deal cycle. Its paid products include ZoomInfo Copilot, ZoomInfo Sales, ZoomInfo Marketing, ZoomInfo Operations, and ZoomInfo Talent, as well as ZoomInfo Lite. The company serves global enterprises, mid-market companies, and down to small businesses that operate in various industry, including software, business services, manufacturing, telecommunications, financial services, media and internet, transportation, education, hospitality, insurance, and real estate. ZoomInfo Technologies Inc. was founded in 2007 and is headquartered in Vancouver, Washington.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 3K people. Revenue per employee of $393K ranks in the above the sector median among Technology peers, improving at 21%/yr — growing workforce leverage. Each employee generates $122K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $37K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 2× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags elevated compensation governance risk (10/10).
financial_summary: ZoomInfo Technologies Inc. is a small-cap technology business with a $1.0B market cap on $1.2B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory. Operating margins are expanding by +2.1pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 4% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 83% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $389M in free cash flow — roughly 31 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.75× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 4.5× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and interest coverage runs at 5.3×.

Management returns a meaningful 40.0% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 13% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

sect: Its 18% operating margin runs 11pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.

mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 66% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 68% below the high.

val: The stock trades 48% below its DCF fair value of $6.79, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 57%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $3.91 to $11.30 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/E 3.1 vs 26.7, EV/EBITDA 7.5 vs 16.4 and P/FCF 2.6 vs 25.4 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 89% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 37.9% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 9.6% (vs the 8% bar).
The 18 covering analysts target $4.58 on average, 31% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 4% falls short of the cost of capital of 8.0%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have been steady (CV 0.25).
It runs a 83% gross margin and converts 31% of revenue into free cash flow, or 22% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 3.75x.
ROE of 8% is amplified by 4.3x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.
It spends 14.6% of revenue on R&D and 9.3% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: Leverage is heavy at 4.5x net debt to EBITDA ($179.9M of cash against $1.3B of debt), with interest covered 5.3x.
Warning signs: an Altman Z of 0.50 in the distress zone, which caps the rating at HOLD.
The current ratio of 0.72 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 4.4% over 3 years and 21.3% over 5 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 24%).
At current returns, reinvesting 47% of profits supports about 2.1% a year of fundamental growth, too little to drive meaningful growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 20.6% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.08 (orders outpacing sales) and a backlog worth 1.0x annual revenue.
Capex runs 2.5x depreciation (6.1% of sales), so it is building capacity for future growth.
own: Insiders own 13.1%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 96%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (8 sales, net $192K sold).
It returns 40.0% a year to shareholders (40.0% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 6.3% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
Short interest is elevated at 13.7% of the float, 5.9 days to cover.
people: With about 3,180 employees, each generates about $393K of revenue, in line with the Technology median, and productivity has risen 21.3% a year.

The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
